query: Controlling for priority and category, which underlying causes explain longer resolution times?

per_column.name: resolution_complexity
per_column.rationale: Directly targets the query's 'underlying causes' of longer resolution times and gives a strong grouping axis. However values assert specific resolution mechanisms (e.g. 'infrastructure_reconfiguration' for a bare 'VPN connection issue') that the short_description does not support; these are invented specifics.

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A useful axis distinct from priority for explaining duration. Some labels are defensible from text ('service_outage' for email not working), but 'intermittent' vs 'individual_access' for similar connectivity descriptions is weakly grounded and inconsistent.

per_column.name: recurrent_issue
per_column.rationale: Recurrence could plausibly explain resolution time, but the source text gives no basis to label a ticket recurrent; nearly all rows are 'true' with no supporting evidence in short_description, indicating fabricated inference.

per_column.name: authentication_or_access_requirement
per_column.rationale: Reasonable causal axis. Mostly derivable from descriptions (VPN/database access -> true; email/wifi -> false), consistent with samples.

per_column.name: hardware_or_software_installation_need
per_column.rationale: Plausible driver of longer times but heavily skewed (482 false) making it near-constant and low leverage. Values shown are defensible from text.

per_column.name: scope_of_impact
per_column.rationale: Scope is a strong candidate cause for duration. Department cases are well grounded, but 'company_wide' being the dominant value and 'single_user' assigned to a plain 'VPN connection issue' involve inference beyond what many terse descriptions state.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with existing 'assigned_to' original column, adding little new leverage. Values are plausible but not verifiable from the provided short_description text.

per_column.name: assigned_resolver_consistency
per_column.rationale: Whether opener/resolver match could relate to handoff delays, giving some leverage, but it is derived from other columns rather than text and is somewhat generic.

per_column.name: closure_status_completeness
per_column.rationale: A near-boolean completeness flag largely restating closure fields; little analytical leverage for explaining duration causes.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Well grounded categorisation of the short_description (email/vpn/database/network). Useful, but the query says to control for category, so it partly overlaps the original 'category' column, reducing marginal leverage.

judge.rationale: Several columns (resolution_complexity, scope_of_impact, authentication_requirement, issue_severity_signal) give genuine new axes to explain longer resolution times beyond priority and category, which is exactly what the query needs. Weaknesses: some columns are redundant with originals (assigned_technician vs assigned_to, issue_category vs category) or near-constant/restated (closure_status_completeness). Groundedness is mixed: categorisation-style columns read the description soundly, but 'resolution_complexity' and especially 'recurrent_issue' assert confident specifics (mechanisms, recurrence) that the terse source text does not support, indicating hallucinated inference.
